outcome.shown: The seasons on Earth are caused by the planet's axial tilt of approximately 23.5 degrees relative to its orbital path around the Sun. As Earth completes its year-long orbit, this tilt remains fixed in space, meaning different hemispheres receive varying angles and intensities of sunlight at different times of the year. When a hemisphere is tilted toward the Sun, it experiences summer due to more direct solar radiation and longer daylight hours; conversely, when it is tilted away, it experiences winter with less direct sunlight and shorter days. The transitional periods between these extremes produce spring and autumn, resulting in the continuous cycle of the seasons.
